title: Ode to the Golden Apple
subtitle: To be misunderstood is the fate of every apple.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: A song descends from Olympus,

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: Of an apple gold as the sun.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: For secrets held in Hesperides bough,

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: Stirs to conflict the fairest and foul.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Must I really be up so high, Captain? Between the thin air and the fumes from this paint, I'm beginning to feel woozy.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Well, whose fault is that for shaking off your old coat?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Though you do look smashing in gold, mate!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. APPLe, are you high enough to be visible to the crowd?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: ... I'm bloody well high enough to be sick.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Excellent, good luck!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hello, Athens! Allow me to direct your eyes to the skies!

items.speaker: Athenian I
items.text: By Zeus—is that a golden apple?!

items.speaker: Athenian II
items.text: An offering like that might convince the gods to cleanse our city of its sorrow and pain ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oi! Wouldn't you like to be the first one to have their mitts on it? Too bad, I'm getting to it first!

items.speaker: Athenian III
items.text: We must offer that apple to the great Dionysos!

items.speaker: Athenian I
items.text: After her! Don't let that strange foreigner steal our golden apple!

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Well done.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Is this also part of your plan?
The crowd has emptied from the square, chasing the golden apple as it floats away. Those that remain here have only one purpose and are eager to return to it.
Alexios's sight is still fixed on the strange fruit as it disappears into the distance. Slowly, he returns his eyes back to the fight before him.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: I don't know by what means you've done this, but don't presume it changes anything.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Let's put these tricks aside, Kassandra.
Kassandra's knuckles turn white from her tightened grip.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: This isn't what I want, Alexios. We are family.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: But it is what I want.
Sword meets spear in a shower of sparks; their battle has begun.
Clang! The Sword of Damokles is sent out from Deimos's hand, and beside it a broken spear is pierced into the soft ground.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Impossible ...

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Nothing is impossible. Not even redemption.
Kassandra's voice is winded but calm. She braces her stance as her legs shake from exhaustion.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: You have a chance to choose another path, Alexios.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Bury the name "Deimos" and return to who you really are, brother.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Put the past aside, and you may still have a chance to best me in the future.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: The fates have already made their choice; our destinies must take us on different paths.
He reaches for the sword, breathing deep against the pain, but then as an eagle retracts his talons, he sheathes it.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: You will never know a moment of peace, sister. I will kill you and all you hold dear.

items.speaker: Alexios
items.text: Retreat!
Smoke bombs erupt across the plaza as the cultists flee in every direction.
As the clangor of battle fades at last, Perikles emerges from behind a pillar.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: You've saved me, Eagle Bearer, and indeed all of Athens.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: We cannot be hasty in claiming victory, Perikles. The enemy is not yet defeated.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: My brother will return.
She presses her hands on her temple, feeling the dull throb of her adrenaline.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: The fates will bring what they will, but for now the battle is won, my friend.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: Athens will survive another day, thanks to you.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I have done my duty as a misthios, nothing more. Besides—

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I said that my services would cost you.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: Of course. On matters of payment, my honor is unwavering.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: But for now, you must rest until you can make your way to Kos Island to see Hippokrates about your injuries. The journey ahead is long, but they say his skills surpass even Apollo's ... Oh, and on the subject of the gods.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Yes?
Perikles looks out at the horizon.

items.speaker: Perikles
items.text: What is the nature of that talking apple that appeared over the plaza? Could it be the same golden apple spoken of in myth?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Maybe so.
She stretches out her sore muscles. As she does, a familiar bard appears, racing toward her with a joyful expression.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: Oh, if it isn't my dear Kassandra. I wonder if you caught much of the ode I sang?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Euphonia? Well, I admit I've developed a new appreciation for your music ...

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: I won't be so stingy with my applause in the future.

items.speaker: Bard
items.text: Wonderful! Does that mean you'll finally let me compose a song about you, Kassandra?

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: No, not that. Never that.
A good mercenary tries to never reveal her weaknesses.

items.speaker: Kassandra
items.text: Now ... Have you seen our friends?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ver-Vertin, how-how much longer ... until we can stop ... running?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I ca-can't go on much longer ...
Matching the concern, a nervous and sickly voice wafts down from the sky.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This APPLe is very much interested in your answer ...
Yet the frantic mob chasing them does not yet seem to have diminished.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Just hang in there.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Keep a stiff upper lip you two, and if all goes well, I'll make sure to requisition some sherry and Dr. Papper to celebrate.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And a whole bunch of records!
